---
title: "Single-cell: comparing conditions"
description: >
  Does a condition change which cells are present, or where they sit on the
  embedding? summarize_group_meta(), get_meta_pivot(),
  plot_composition_scatter() and DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit().
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** between two conditions, do the proportions of cell types change,
and where on the embedding are cells gained or lost?

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `summarize_group_meta()` | counts and proportions per group, condition (and sample) |
| `get_meta_pivot()` | a quick two-way table of two metadata columns |
| `plot_composition_scatter()` | proportion of each group in one condition against another |
| `DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit()` | where on an embedding a condition has more or fewer cells |

These plots describe differences; they do not test them. Cells from one
sample are not independent replicates, so tests of composition must use
samples (e.g. propeller, scCODA, Milo).

**Data:** 8,000 PBMCs from [Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042),
8 donors, each sampled as control and after 6 h of interferon-β (IFN-β): 16
samples.

```{r data}
pbmc <- docs_kang()
```

## Counting cells

`summarize_group_meta()` counts the cells of each group per condition (and
per sample with `sample.by`) and their proportion of the condition's cells.
It takes a Seurat object or its metadata.

```{r summarize}
comp <- summarize_group_meta(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", split.by = "condition")
head(comp)
```

```{r summarize-samples}
per_sample <- summarize_group_meta(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)
head(per_sample, 3)
```

`get_meta_pivot()` gives a two-way table of any two columns, as counts or as
percentages of rows, columns or the total:

```{r pivot}
get_meta_pivot(pbmc$cell_type, pbmc$condition, type = "count")
get_meta_pivot(
    pbmc$cell_type,
    pbmc$condition,
    type = "percent",
    margin = "column"
)
```

## Composition scatter

Each group's proportion in one condition (x) against the other (y), with the
y = x line: groups above it are more abundant in the y condition.

```{r composition}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    x = "Control",
    y = "IFN-beta"
)
```

Six hours of IFN-β leave the cell type composition almost unchanged: all
cell types lie on the line. The response is a change of state, seen in the
expression of interferon-stimulated genes (see
[Expression across groups](sc-expression.html)).

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `sample.by`

Proportions per sample, each point the mean of a condition's samples, so that
every donor counts the same. The horizontal bar is computed from the samples
of the x condition and the vertical bar from those of the y condition:
`error` chooses the SEM (default), the SD of the samples, or a 95% confidence
interval of the mean (`"ci95"`, mean ± t(0.975, n - 1) × SEM, t-based since
there are few samples per condition).

```{r comp-samples}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)
```

```{r comp-ci}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor",
    error = "ci95",
    log = TRUE
)
```

#### `log` and `fold.lines`

Log axes spread rare groups; `fold.lines = 2` draws y = 2x and y = x / 2:

```{r comp-log}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    log = TRUE,
    fold.lines = 2
)
```

#### `value = "count"`

Numbers of cells instead of proportions:

```{r comp-count}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    value = "count",
    log = TRUE
)
```

#### `facet.by`

One panel per level of a third column, with proportions computed within
each, e.g. within lymphoid and myeloid cells:

```{r comp-facet}
is_lymphoid <- pbmc$cell_type %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T", "NK", "B")
pbmc$lineage <- factor(
    ifelse(is_lymphoid, "Lymphoid", "Myeloid"),
    levels = c("Lymphoid", "Myeloid")
)
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    facet.by = "lineage",
    panel.width = 2.2,
    cells = colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type != "Megakaryocyte"]
)
```

## Density difference on the embedding

`DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit()` estimates the density of cells of each
condition on the embedding (normalized, so cell numbers do not matter) and
draws the difference from a reference condition: magenta where the compared
condition has relatively more cells, blue where it has fewer. The colour
scale is centred on 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own
extreme. With `sample.by`, each sample's density is computed separately and
averaged, so one large sample cannot drive the map.

What the map means depends on the embedding. On the **integrated** UMAP
(Harmony over condition), cells of both conditions are aligned by cell type,
so the map shows shifts within cell types:

```{r density}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)
```

On the UMAP **before integration**, IFN-β-stimulated cells of every type sit
apart from their controls, and the map shows that response as a separation:

```{r density-raw}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    reduction = "umap.unintegrated",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `measure = "log2ratio"`

The log2 ratio of the two densities instead of their difference: fold
changes, which also show sparse regions.

```{r density-ratio}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    measure = "log2ratio"
)
```

#### `draw = "raster"` and `contour`

The density difference drawn as a continuous surface, with contours of the
density of all cells:

```{r density-raster}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    draw = "raster",
    contour = TRUE
)
```

#### `density.adjust`

The bandwidth multiplier: below 1 resolves smaller regions, above 1 smooths
more.

```{r density-adjust}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    density.adjust = 0.5
)
```
